lines.t: There. It'll stay open for good. Catch a verdant friend when you can — the wild's full of them.
Murmurwood's past the roots. Mind the hollow trees; they talk back when the wind's up.
Rootgate's closed since the hum faded. You'll want Oriel in Larkhollow to show you how glyphs work first. Everyone starts there.
Rootgate's closed since the hum faded. A verdant kin could coax it. Got one?
If not, no shame in it. That glyph wants a verdant voice. I'll lend you mine — just this once.
Listen. All four hollows, humming in thirds. I haven't heard that since I was your age. Thank you.
You woke them. All four. The whole wood just breathed out — did you feel it?
Brass Chimes, from the wardens' store, and some good Salves. You've earned both twice over.
Four hollows: by the Chordstone to the west, the east grove, the far west hill, and the little one near the engineers' tents.
A verdant, electric or fire voice will wake one. No such kin? A glowcap works too — they grow along the old paths.
Since those engineers clamped their coil on the Great Tree, four of the hollows have gone mute. Just… stopped.
A hollow tree that won't hum is a tree that's forgotten it's alive. Would you wake them for me?
Murmurwood's hollow trees hum when the wind passes through. Most days it's a lullaby. Today it's a complaint.
There's a strange tapping from the Great Hollow Tree, east of here. Brass on bark. I don't like it.
We're engineers, not bandits. A stone that sings on its own is a hazard. We make it safe. That's all.
The Magister says unregulated stones are how people get hurt. She's usually right about hazards.
Both of my engineers, off the job. I'll have to note this on the work order. Obstruction of service.
We're engineers, not bandits. A stone that sings on its own is a hazard. We make it safe. That's all.
Fine. We'll pack the coil. The wardens can have their hall back. For now.
Licensed survey, Tuner. Stand clear of the coil, please.
If you have a complaint, my engineers will take it. They're right there. They love complaints.
Wren's Keynote on your belt! Then the canopy bridge is yours. We've lowered it over the ravine — north, past the old path.
The coil's off the Great Tree and the doors are open. Cantor Wren is waiting inside. Tread softly — the floor listens.
Hall's shut, I'm afraid. Can't hold a trial with engineers clamping brass to the very tree it grows in.
If someone were to have a firm word with them — a battling sort of word — I'd open these doors in a heartbeat.
